title: Snickerdoodle Cookies
metaDescription: Cream of tartar isn't optional flavor trivia here — it's what gives snickerdoodles their signature tang and soft, crackled-top texture that baking powder alone can't fully replicate.
author: Laura Bennett
keywords: snickerdoodle cookies, cinnamon sugar cookies, classic cookies

steps.name: Mix dry ingredients
steps.text: Whisk together flour, cream of tartar, baking soda and salt in a bowl.

steps.name: Cream butter and sugar
steps.text: Beat butter with 1 cup of the sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes.

steps.name: Add eggs and vanilla
steps.text: Beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla, until fully combined.

steps.name: Combine and shape
steps.text: Gradually mix in the dry ingredients until just combined. In a small bowl, mix the remaining 1/2 cup sugar with the cinnamon. Roll dough into 1-inch balls and coat each in the cinnamon sugar.

steps.name: Bake
steps.text: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C). Place balls on a lined baking sheet, spaced 2 inches apart, and bake for 8-10 minutes until the edges are set but the centers still look soft — they will puff and crackle on top.

tips.question: What does cream of tartar actually do here?
tips.answer: It reacts with the baking soda to give snickerdoodles their signature slight tang and helps create the classic soft, chewy texture with crackled tops — it's not interchangeable with just using more baking powder.

tips.question: Can I make these without cream of tartar?
tips.answer: You can substitute 2 tsp baking powder in place of the cream of tartar and baking soda combined, though the classic tangy flavor will be milder.

tips.question: Why do the tops crack?
tips.answer: The crackled top is normal for snickerdoodles and comes from the dough spreading and setting around the sugar coating as it bakes — it's a sign the cookie baked correctly, not a mistake.

storyIntro: Snickerdoodles get their distinct tangy edge from cream of tartar, an ingredient most other cookies skip entirely — it's the one thing that separates a true snickerdoodle from a plain cinnamon sugar cookie.
Rolling the dough balls in cinnamon sugar before baking is what gives them that crackled, sparkly top.
storyNote: Don't skip the cream of tartar or swap it out casually — it's responsible for both the tangy flavor and the classic soft-crackled texture that defines a snickerdoodle.
